full_judgment:
Md Ruhul Amin J: This petition has been filed seeking review of the judgment dated May 15, 2005 in Civil Appeal No. 1 of 1999 allowing the same. The civil appeal was filed against the judgment dated November 3, 1991 of the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 448 of 1988 making the Rule absolute. The writ petition was filed challenging the legality of the judgment dated January 3, 1988 of the Court of Settlement in Case No. 119 of 1987 (Kha-145-Tinshed Colony, Block-D) Quarter No. 169 (Holding No. 38), Tinshed Colony, Mohammadpur, Dhaka. The said case was filed challenging the listing of the property in the 'Kha' list and publishing thereof in the Bangladesh Gazette (Extra-ordinary) dated September 23, 1986. The list in respect of the property in question and the publication of the list was made as per provision of the Ordinance No. 54 of 1985. The Court of Settlement by its judgment dismissed the case holding that the property in question is an abandoned property within the meaning of the provision of President Order No. 16 of 1972 and the Provision of Ordinance No. 54 of 1985 and that including of the property in question in the 'Kha' list and publication of the said list in the Bangladesh Gazette is quite legal. 

 2. The writ petition was filed challenging the aforementioned judgment of the Court of Settlement. The High Court Division upon making the Rule absolute declared that the property in question. is not an abandoned property and the property has been listed in the 'Kha' list without lawful authority and, as such, the same has no legal effect. The High Court Division further directed the Government to exclude the property in question from the list of abandoned property. 

 3. It was the case of the petitioner (Rowshan Ara Begum) before the Court of Settlement that the property in question was allotted to one Sahera Khatun, widow of late Abdul Gafur on August 24, 1957 and said Sahera Khatun orally gifted the property on April 14, 1973 to her daughter Anwari Khatun, that Sahera Khatun in confirmation of the oral gift affirmed an affidavit before the Magistrate, 1st Class, Dhaka on July 14, 1973, In the affidavit it was stated that Sahera Khatun gifted the property in presence of Amanullah Munsif, Abdul Hashim and Md Riazuddin, that Anwari Khatun on October 22, 1979 by registered deed transferred the property in question to the petitioner before the Court of Settlement, that after purchasing the property the petitioner got her name mutated in the records of the different authorities, obtained approval from the RAJUK for making construction and also obtained loan from the House Building Finance Corporation and made construction in the property in question. It was the case of the petitioner that she was in possession of the property in question and that she was surprised to see the property in the 'Kha' list of the abandoned property published in the Bangladesh Gazette as per provision of Ordinance No. 54 of 1985. 

 4. The Government contested the case before the Court of Settlement by making submissions that Sahera Khatun and her daughter Anwari Khatun during the war of liberation left the property in question without making any arrangement for its management and supervision and that after war of liberation their whereabouts were not known and that on the date of promulgation of PO 16 of 1972 whereabouts of Sahera Khatun and Anwari Khatun were not known, that the petitioner's case of making gift of the property by Sahera Khatun to her daughter Anwari Khatun on April 14, 1973 and affirming of an affidavit by Sahera Khatun in confirmation of the oral gift said to have been made by her, to her daughter Anwari Khatun are all got up story, that the claim of the petitioner that Sahera Khatun had a daughter Anwari Khatun is also a got up story, that petitioner got her name mutated in different records of the Government unauthorisedly and also upon resorting to practice which has no sanction of law, that mutation in the record of the Government was made without approval of the competent authority. The Court of Settlement dismissed the case observing, amongst others, "No oral evidence has been adduced by the petitioner that Sahera Khatun was present and her whereabouts were known after liberation at least on and from 28-2-72. The alleged oral gift has not been formally proved before this Court nor the 3 witnesses of the oral gift mentioned in the affidavit dated 14-7-73 have been examined in this case ............... In the absence of evidence to this effect it is difficult to accept the case of the petitioner that Sahera Khatun was present after liberation and that the oral gift by Sahera Khatun was genuine, rather her whereabouts were not known and oral gift was not genuine. 

 5. From the judgment of the Court of Settlement it appears that thee was no case of the petitioner before the Court of Settlement that the property in question was listed in the 'Kha' list without serving notice on her. 

 6. As against the judgment of the Court of Settlement the petitioner moved the High Court Division in writ jurisdiction and obtained Rule. The petitioner before the High Court Division, amongst others, contended that the property was listed in the 'Kha' list without serving any notice. The High Court Division while making the Rule absolute observed "Unless the prerequisites as mentioned in section 5(1)(2)(sic) of the Ordinance are fulfilled, the jurisdiction of the Court of Settlement ceases to operate and the respondents are bound to prove that the properties so enlisted in the Official Gazette are abandoned properties. If this burden could be discharged by the Government then of course, it shifts or reverts to the petitioner to prove that the property is not an abandoned property............................The Court of Settlement misplaced the onus upon the petitioner to prove that the whereabouts of the original owner was not known to the government......................The fact that gift was made by Sahera Khatun in favour of her daughter Anwari Khatun having been affirmed on oath by an affidavit before the Magistrate, 1st Class, the learned Court of Settlement ought not to have challenged the same as no such challenge had been offered by the government before the Court of Settlement. The findings of the Court of Settlement having not been supported by any materials, in our view, the order is without jurisdiction. It is neither stated before the Court of Settlement nor before this Court in the affidavit that any notice has been served upon the petitioner or her vendor for surrendering the properties, the enlistment of the petitioner's property in the official Gazette is illegal and without jurisdiction ....................The enlistment of her property as an abandoned property without answering to the conditions as set forth in section 5 of the Ordinance read with PO 16 of 1972 is without any lawful authority." The High Court Division in its judgment has quoted a finding from the judgment of the Court of Settlement which reads as follows: 

 7. In the aforesaid quotation the word 'not' appears to be a typing mistake, since from the judgment of the Court of Settlement, placed before us at the time of hearing of the review petition, it is seen the aforesaid portion of the judgment reads as follows: 

 8. In the other part of the judgment of the Court of Settlement it has been observed "In the absence of evidence to this effect it is difficult to accept the case of the petitioner that Sahera Khatun was present after liberation and that the oral gift by Sahera Khatun was genuine, rather her whereabouts were not known and oral gift was not genuine. 

 9. The learned Counsel for the petitioner in support of the prayer for review of the judgment of this Court urged that this Court made an error apparent on the face of the record in not noticing the important fact that the property was listed without serving notice on the claimant of the property. In our judgment we addressed the aforesaid contention of the petitioner and we observed "The question of service or non-service of notice is a question of fact and determination thereof is required upon consideration of the evidence brought on record by the parties." We have observed in our judgment that before the Court of Settlement the petitioner did not take any stand or, in other words, did not make any contention as to listing of the property without serving notice and in the background thereof in our judgment we observed that the contention made as to non-service of notice in enlisting the property in question as abandoned property merits no consideration. 

 11. In the instant case while the property was listed in the 'Kha' list of the abandoned buildings and published in the Bangladesh Gazette the claimant of the property moved the Court of Settlement under section 7 of Ordinance No. 54 of 1985. 

 12. The provision of section 7 requires the claimant of the property to establish "that the building is not an abandoned property and has not been vested in the Government under the President's Order or that his right or interest in the building has not been affected by the provisions of that Order." The Court of Settlement dismissed the petitioner's case on the finding that the petitioner failed to establish that at the material time i.e. on February 28, 1972 Sahera Khatun or, for that matter, Anwari Khatun was present in Bangladesh. This fact having not been established the Court of Settlement held that the property in question on the promulgation of PO 16 of 1972 became an abandoned property and vested in the Government. It is in PO 16 of 1972 that transfer made after the property assumed the character of abandoned property has no legal coverage. It is seen from the judgment of the Court of Settlement that no evidence was led from the side of the claimant of the property to establish the fact that Sahera Khatun or for that matter Anwari Khatun from whom the petitioner said to have purchased the property was in Bangladesh after liberation of Bangladesh and was also present on 28-2-1972. Under the law unless the claimant of the property can establish that the owner of the property from whom he/she made the purchase was present in the Bangladesh at the material time i.e. on 28-2- 1972, the claimant cannot have any relief from the Court of Settlement or, in other words, cannot have the direction from the Court of Settlement for delisting of the property from the list of abandoned property as published in the Bangladesh Gazette either in the "Ka' list or in the 'Kha' list as per provision of the Ordinance No. 54 of 1985. In the instant case the petitioner having not been able to establish before the Court of Settlement that the claimant of the property or for that matter her vendor Anwari Khatun were present in Bangladesh on 28-2-1972 and consequent thereupon the property having had assumed the character of abandoned Petitioners property, the listing of the property in question, even if without service of notice as per provision of Ordinance No. 54 of 1985, is not material as the property because of non-service of notice for listing in the list of abandoned properties would not cease to be an abandoned property and consequent there upon the claim of title made by the petitioner in the property in question is not legally sustainable or, in other words, the petitioner cannot raise any claim of title in the property in question since said property is an abandoned property. The ground contending which review of our judgment is sought merits no consideration.
